article.title: How to Replace a Door Knob (Interior or Exterior)
article.summary: Replace an interior or exterior door knob in about 15 minutes: pick the right function and backset, swap the latch, and align it with the strike plate.
article.body:
A sticky, loose or dated door knob is a quick swap with one screwdriver. Most new knobs fit standard U.S. door holes. This guide covers passage, privacy and keyed knobs and levers.

Steps

  1. Pick the right function and measure the backset

    Choose the function: passage (no lock, for halls and closets), privacy (push-button lock, for bedrooms and baths) or keyed entry (exterior doors). Measure from the door edge to the center of the knob hole. That's the backset, usually 2-3/8 in or 2-3/4 in; most new latches adjust to both.

    Done right: the box lists your function and backset, and the hole in the door is the standard 2-1/8 in.

  2. Remove the old knob

    On the inside knob, look for two screws on the rose (round plate). Remove them and pull both knobs apart. If you see no screws, find a small slot or hole on the knob's neck, press it with a small screwdriver, and slide the knob off; the rose then pops or twists off to reveal the screws.

    Done right: both knobs are off and only the latch remains in the door edge.

  3. Swap the latch

    Remove the two screws on the door edge and pull out the old latch. Set the new latch to your backset, then slide it in with the angled side of the bolt facing the direction the door closes. Screw it in flush with the door edge.

    Done right: the latch plate sits flush, and the slanted bolt faces the door frame when you close the door.

  4. Install the new knobs

    Slide the exterior (or keyed) knob in from the outside so its spindle passes through the latch. Line up the interior knob on the other side and drive in the two long screws, alternating so the knobs pull together evenly. Snug them, but don't overtighten or the knob will bind.

    Done right: both knobs turn smoothly and the latch snaps back on its own when released.

  5. Test the latch and adjust the strike

    Close the door gently. The latch should click into the strike plate on the frame without you pushing. If it catches, loosen the strike plate and shift it up or down, or file the opening slightly. Fill stripped screw holes with glue-dipped toothpicks and redrive the screws.

    Done right: the door latches with a light push and doesn't rattle when closed.

Call a locksmith or carpenter if: the door has a non-standard bore, a mortise lock (a large rectangular lock body inside the door), or the door has sagged so much that the latch misses the strike by more than 1/4 in.

FAQ

Are door knobs universal?

Most U.S. knobs fit a standard 2-1/8 in bore hole with a 2-3/8 or 2-3/4 in backset. Older or European doors may differ.

How do I remove a door knob with no visible screws?

Find the small slot or pinhole on the knob's neck, press it with a small screwdriver or pick, and pull the knob off. The rose then comes off to reveal the screws.

Which way does the latch go?

The slanted side of the latch bolt faces the direction the door closes, so it slides along the strike plate.

Can I replace a knob with a lever?

Yes, levers fit the same standard holes, and they're easier for kids, older adults and anyone carrying something.
